title: Auxin Extraction and Purification Based on Recombinant Aux/IAA Proteins
author: Su, Luo, et al.
materials: Bacterial cells were collected and resuspended in PBS (pH 7.4). Cells were disrupted by ultrasonification. Supernatant was collected for target protein purification after centrifugation at 20,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C. For insect expression, the medium was collected from 100-mL cultures by centrifugation, since the recombinant protein was secreted into the medium. Supernatant was concentrated to less than 5 mL by centrifugation at 7500 g for 10 min in Amicon Ultra-4 Centrifugal Filter Devices with a 50 kDa nominal molecular weight limit (NMWL) from Millipore at 4 °C. Condensed culture medium was diluted 5 times in PBS to prepare it for protein purification. Protein solution was added to a column pre-filled with GST Sefirose™ resin at a speed of 1 mL/min. The purified target proteins remained trapped in the column after it was washed with 5 resin volumes of PBS.

steps.title: Lyse bacterial cells and collect supernatant
steps.instruction: Resuspend harvested bacterial cells in PBS (pH 7.4), disrupt them by ultrasonication, then centrifuge at 20,000 g for 10 min at 4 °C and collect the supernatant for recombinant protein purification.

steps.title: Process insect‑cell culture supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 100 mL insect‑cell culture to pellet cells, keep the medium, and concentrate the supernatant to <5 mL using an Amicon Ultra‑4 centrifugal filter device (50 kDa NMWL, Millipore) at 7,500 g for 10 min at 4 °C. Dilute the concentrate 5‑fold with PBS before loading onto the GST resin column.

steps.title: Prepare GST‑resin gravity column
steps.instruction: Fill a cartridge with GST Sefirose™ resin, equilibrate the resin with PBS (pH 7.4). This gravity column will be used to immobilize GST‑Aux/IAA fusion proteins and later to capture IAA.

steps.title: Load recombinant GST‑Aux/IAA protein onto column
steps.instruction: Apply the protein solution (from bacterial lysate or diluted insect supernatant) to the pre‑filled GST resin column at a flow rate of 1 mL min⁻¹. Wash the column with 5 resin volumes of PBS to remove unbound material, leaving GST‑Aux/IAA protein bound to the resin.

steps.title: Bind labeled IAA to immobilized protein
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1 ng ²H₅‑IAA in 5 mL PBS (pH 7.4) and add the solution to the gravity column containing purified GST‑IAA1, GST‑IAA7, or GST‑IAA28. Incubate at 4 °C for 10 min, 30 min, and 60 min (separate columns or sequential elutions) to allow IAA binding. Collect the flow‑through for later analysis.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 ng ²H₅‑IAA in 5 mL PBS to column.
Incubate at 4 °C for 10 min; collect outlet.
Incubate at 4 °C for 30 min; collect outlet.
Incubate at 4 °C for 60 min; collect outlet.

steps.title: Elute IAA from column
steps.instruction: Elute bound IAA by passing 3 column volumes of high‑pH buffer (HPB: 0.1 M Tris‑HCl, pH 8.4) through the column at the same flow rate. Alternatively, use low‑pH buffer (LPB, pH 4.5) or GST exchange buffer (0.1 M Tris‑HCl plus 10 mM reduced glutathione). Collect the eluate, which contains IAA, recombinant protein, Tris‑HCl, and NaCl and is suitable for LC‑MS/MS quantification.

steps.title: Quantify IAA by LC‑MS/MS
steps.instruction: Analyze the eluate with HPLC‑MS/MS (or LC‑MS/MS) using a standard curve to determine the concentration of IAA in the sample.
